root_cause.text: The xt_tcpudp and xt_dccp option-walking loops in netfilter x_tables dereference `op[i + 1]` without first checking whether `i` is already at the last byte of the option buffer, causing an out-of-bounds 1-byte tail read when the final option is not a single-byte kind.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `i == optlen - 1` guards before `i += op[i + 1] ? : 1` in both `tcp_find_option()` and `dccp_find_option()`, and the commit message explicitly says walkers using `i += op[i + 1] ? : 1` “can read `op[i + 1]` past the end of the option area.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix an out-of-bounds option parsing access in dccp_find_option() by guarding the final-byte case.
intent_record.what: The loop condition inside dccp_find_option() was changed so that the index is incremented when op[i] is less than 2 or when i is the last byte in the option buffer, and the ternary expression spacing in i += op[i + 1] ? : 1 was adjusted.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from reading op[i + 1] when i already points to the final byte of the buffer, avoiding an out-of-bounds access while scanning options.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix tcp_find_option() to avoid out-of-bounds option parsing at the end of the buffer.
intent_record.what: The loop in tcp_find_option() changed its iteration logic: the single-line condition `if (op[i] < 2) i++; else i += op[i+1]?:1;` was replaced with a multi-line conditional that increments by 1 when `op[i] < 2` or when `i == optlen - 1`, otherwise it advances by `op[i + 1] ?: 1`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the code from reading `op[i + 1]` when the current index is at the last byte of the options buffer, avoiding an out-of-bounds access while preserving the existing option scanning behavior for valid option lengths.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable option-walking loop is present in `tcp_find_option()`: `for (i = 0; i < optlen; ) { ... else i += op[i+1]?:1; }`. This dereferences `op[i+1]` without any prior check that `i` is not already at the last byte of the option buffer, which matches the described out-of-bounds 1-byte tail read. The same pattern is used in the TCP option parser; no guard like `i + 1 < optlen` or equivalent fix is present. The function body is sufficient to determine this because it shows the full loop and its bounds handling.
